candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Determine a common denominator and rewrite one or more fractional parts as equivalent fractions before subtraction when denominators do not already match.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S01, B.S01, and C.S01 are effectively identical in name, scope, and examples: all cover making unlike denominators match before subtraction.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite a whole number or mixed number into a subtraction-ready form, such as expressing a whole as a whole plus zero fractional part or converting an improper mixed form to a standard mixed number.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S02, B.S02, and C.S02 all describe preparatory rewriting of whole numbers or mixed numbers into a form suitable for subtraction, excluding borrowing/regrouping.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Subtract fractional parts once they share a common denominator, including fraction-only problems and the fractional components of mixed-number subtraction.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: C.S03 isolates fraction-part subtraction as its own concept, whereas A and B fold this operation into a broader combined subtraction skill that also includes whole-part subtraction.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Subtract the whole-number components in a mixed-number or whole-number subtraction setup, whether done alone or alongside fraction subtraction.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: C.S04 separates whole-part subtraction from fraction subtraction. In A and B, whole-part subtraction is included inside the broader aligned-subtraction skill rather than treated as a standalone concept.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Subtract quantities once they are in compatible form, including subtracting numerators over a shared denominator and subtracting whole-number parts in mixed-number problems.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S03 and B.S03 are direct matches and both combine whole-part and fraction-part subtraction into one skill. C splits this broader concept into C.S03 and C.S04, so no single C skill is equivalent to the full combined concept.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Regroup one whole as fractional units and adjust the whole-number part when the fractional part of the minuend is too small to continue subtraction.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S04, B.S04, and C.S05 all describe the same regrouping/borrowing action in mixed-number or whole-minus-fraction subtraction.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Reduce the subtraction result to lowest terms or simplify it to a whole number or zero when appropriate.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S05, B.S05, and C.S06 are the same post-subtraction simplification concept, with only minor wording differences.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Combine the computed whole-number and fractional parts, or recognize that only a fraction or whole number remains, to state the final result.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S06, B.S06, and C.S07 all cover assembling the final mixed number, fraction, or integer after computation.

alignment_summary: The three codebooks align strongly on denominator matching, normalization, borrowing, simplification, and final answer composition. The main structural difference is that Experts A and B use one broader subtraction skill for both whole and fraction parts, while Expert C splits that broader operation into two separate skills: subtract aligned fractions and subtract whole parts. All skill IDs from all experts were mapped exactly once.
